name: The Nuclear Century: Fear, Power and the Bomb
description: From glowing rays in a Paris laboratory to the bomb, the reactor and the accidents that followed: how the splitting of the atom shaped the modern world.

checkpoints.name: Rays in the dark
checkpoints.note: Rontgen's X-rays and Becquerel's accidental find of radioactivity set off a hunt in which Pierre and Marie Curie isolated new elements, and Rutherford began to show that atoms change and have an inner structure.

checkpoints.name: Mapping the atom
checkpoints.note: Bohr placed electrons in orbits around Rutherford's nucleus, and Chadwick found the neutron, a new tool for probing it. Fermi bombarded uranium with neutrons, and in 1938 Hahn and Strassmann found a strange result that Meitner and Frisch explained as fission.

checkpoints.name: The race for the bomb
checkpoints.note: Szilard and Einstein warned of a chain reaction. Fermi's pile in Chicago proved it, and the Manhattan Project, led by General Groves with Oppenheimer directing the Los Alamos laboratory, built weapons tested at Trinity and used on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

checkpoints.name: Fear and promise
checkpoints.note: The Atomic Age brought hydrogen bombs, Cold War standoffs such as the Cuban Missile Crisis, a treaty to limit the spread of weapons, and the first reactor feeding a grid at Obninsk. Godzilla gave the fear a monster's face.

checkpoints.name: Accidents and fusion dreams
checkpoints.note: Three Mile Island, Chernobyl and Fukushima shook trust in nuclear power and left zones where people cannot live. Meanwhile tokamaks and ITER pursue fusion, the cleaner power of the stars.
